analysis:
The only change in this PR is one added documentation row in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 414) for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. It describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. A 128-token shader-cache probe runs twice, and the shape cells run only on a cold cache, within 20 seconds per engine. The row says it trains no rate or counter and is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No code is changed in the supplied evidence, so I observed no regression in authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or key custody.

Relevant threat-model touchpoints are TB-007, T-029 and T-041. The warmup is bounded to 20 seconds per engine, and the row names disable values (0/false/no/off). It is described as running at load time on synthetic probe tokens, not on consumer prompts, so it should not touch A-001 plaintext or the prefix-cache tiers (T-041). The documented passthrough to launchd is a low-risk operator toggle that can only disable or skip the probe, not widen trust.

Unverified contracts that the code-side pass should confirm: (1) ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupMode exists and behaves as documented, (2) the warmup does not populate or donate to the SSD prefix cache or reuse real user KV, and (3) LaunchAgent passthrough includes the variable. These are documentation-versus-code questions, not evidence of a vulnerability. The rest of the file (lines 1-353 and 354-514) is unchanged context. I found nothing there that this PR alters, and I did not re-audit it.
